extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations. It covers 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark aggregates existing datasets across four task families (speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval) covering 102 languages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Speech data covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, sourced from existing datasets like Fleurs, MLS, and VoxPopuli.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: There is a performance disparity across geographical language groups, with models performing significantly better on Western European languages compared to Sub-Saharan African or South Asian languages due to imbalances in unlabeled data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Because the test sets are publicly available, there is a risk of overfitting if users do not follow the honor system of using the development set for tuning. Additionally, there remains a significant performance gap between high-resource and low-resource language families.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to foster the development of speech technologies for under-represented languages, giving these speakers an equal voice online and enabling them to share their culture globally.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains speech data categorized by language and geography, covering 102 languages across multiple language families and geographical regions (e.g., Western European, Sub-Saharan African, South Asian).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for the evaluation (testing) and fine-tuning of multilingual speech representations across recognition, translation, classification, and retrieval tasks. Usage guidelines specify that hyperparameter search must be done on the dev set, and restrict the use of external supervision during fine-tuning.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The benchmark allows and encourages data augmentation, specifically using TTS (Text-to-Speech) augmentation and training text-augmented speech models.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The benchmark encourages filtering methods to adapt large unlabeled text datasets to specific tasks and domains.

name.evidence: We introduce XTREME-S , a new benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages.

description.evidence: XTREME-S covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval. Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: we report average character and word error rates on Fleurs, MLS and VoxPopuli.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families... we report average character and word error rates on Fleurs, MLS and VoxPopuli.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We observe in Table 4 that results are much better on the Western European group (with 11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Test sets are available in open-source and are not hidden to the public. We trust practitioners to perform all hyperparameter search and checkpoint selection on the dev set, and eventually report performance on the test set.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: It covers 102 diverse languages spanning more than 10 language families... results are much better on the Western European group... than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African... or South Asian

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: XTREME-S is meant to be a more exhaustive, thorough and complete evaluation of learned speech representations. [...] At ﬁne-tuning time, we ask that submissions leverage only the ASR supervision of each task.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We encourage the use of these datasets for learning language models, for training text-augmented speech models, or using TTS augmentation for example.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We hope the community can also develop smarter ways to adapt these very large unlabeled text datasets to each particular task and domain through ﬁltering methods.
